summary: Explore conference booking patterns, compare prediction approaches and communicate results through a graphical application.
decision: Preserve the separate analysis, imputation and modelling components. Data preparation must be fitted within each training fold so future observations cannot influence past predictions.
tradeoff: A desktop interface supports the original local analysis workflow. A browser edition improves discoverability, while executing the original fitted models would require a separately secured Python service.
contract: Input contracts should name event identifier, booking-created date and observation cutoff. Split by event and time, account for zero-booking weeks, and track the provenance of every imputed value.
limits: The browser workbench uses seven invented weekly counts and descriptive z-scores. It does not run the original regression/classification models or measure their performance.
